page: Amazon Web Services c8ib.metal-96xl is a bare-metal, compute-optimized instance built on the x86_64 architecture. Powered by dedicated Intel processors running at clock speeds of up to 3.9 GHz, the server delivers 192 physical cores and 384 execution threads via two threads per core. System memory totals 768.0 GB, providing a standard compute-oriented ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU without the virtualization overhead of a hypervisor.

Network performance is a central capability of this configuration, offering a baseline throughput of 400 Gbps. The server contains no local NVMe storage and does not feature hardware GPU accelerators, necessitating remote block or networked file storage systems for persistent data. This architecture directs resource allocation primarily toward core density, inter-node network bandwidth, and compute throughput.

From an infrastructure investment perspective, c8ib.metal-96xl delivers massive parallelism and high per-socket core capacity, making it a viable solution for scale-out compute jobs where hypervisor overhead must be eliminated. However, workloads requiring massive per-thread memory allocations or extensive local high-IOPS scratch disks will experience architectural constraints without external services. Recommended deployments include distributed high-performance computing (HPC), parallel batch processing, compute-heavy scientific modeling, and distributed cluster nodes.
description: Amazon Web Services c8ib.metal-96xl is a dedicated bare-metal, compute-optimized server engineered for highly parallel processing tasks. Based on x86_64 Intel processors clocking at 3.9 GHz, it supplies 192 physical cores and 384 vCPUs paired with 768.0 GB of memory, establishing a 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio. The platform incorporates a 400 Gbps baseline network interface to facilitate high-throughput cluster communication. It features no integrated local storage and no GPU accelerators, routing data persistence to external storage networks. By removing hypervisor abstraction, c8ib.metal-96xl maximizes direct hardware access and raw multi-threaded throughput. It is technically suited for distributed high-performance computing clusters, intensive financial simulations, batch rendering pipelines, and scalable compute-heavy infrastructure.
